slides.title: My Five Senses
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 1 English, Unit 6: My Five Senses. In this unit you will learn about your five senses — seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching — and the parts of your body you use for each one. You will learn describing words like soft, loud, sweet and cold, and begin to compare things: a tree is tall, a building is taller. Most of all you will explore the world around you, stay curious, and be thankful for all the wonderful things you can sense. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name the five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch.
Point to and name the body parts we use: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands.
Say which sense goes with which body part (“I see with my eyes”).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name the five senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. You will also point to and name the body parts we use: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands. You will also say which sense goes with which body part (“I see with my eyes”). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: see, hear, smell, taste, touch, eyes. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Amal at the Market and Talk about My Five Senses. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Eyes are for seeing
bullets: Point to your eyes and say the whole sentence. Your eyes are the sense that helps you see.
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Eyes are for seeing. Point to your eyes and say the whole sentence. Your eyes are the sense that helps you see. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 - Listen and point. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
